method: rebuilt the code graph (106,383 nodes / 253,647 edges) and reran sinks.py/reach.py; then probed classes not covered in pass 1: caller-sized allocations, extreme/negative numeric MCP arguments against a real ckg mcp process (mcp_probe.py), and traversal depth against this repository's graph

findings.title: caller k sized result slices (makeslice panic)
findings.evidence: keyword_search k=1e15 and evidence_for_intent k=1e15 panicked with makeslice: cap out of range; mcp-go recovered at the transport, but the error reply had id null, leaving the request unanswered
findings.fix: 386ed482: capacity capped at candidate count; k*3 over-fetch guarded

findings.title: large ID lists exceeded SQLite's variable limit
findings.evidence: on this repository's graph an untyped SubgraphByQname/NeighborhoodByQname failed from depth 4 (edges from 86,715 ids: too many SQL variables); NodesByIDs failed for 40,000 IDs, reachable through POST /api/nodes-by-ids within the 4 MiB body cap
findings.fix: d9f7fe13: edge and node lookups split into 400-ID chunks
tests: internal/graph/persist TestLargeIDListsAreQueriedInChunks (RED: too many SQL variables)

findings.title: unbounded caller traversal depth
findings.evidence: cks find_callers/find_callees/get_subgraph and ckg find_callers/find_callees/get_subgraph passed depth unclamped; untyped depth 3 returned about 122,000 edges and depth 5 allocated over 300 MB (impact_of_change already capped at 5)

checked_without_defect: ckg mcp: negative offset, negative k, malformed FTS query and huge max_bodies/prs_per_node/impact_depth/hop_depth returned results or errors without crashing
semantic_search, vector_search and find_branches with k=1e15 did not panic
timing_note: pkg/graph/mcphandlers tests take about 410-420 s with or without the chunking (load about 11); the chunking did not slow them
limits: pass 2 targeted size, depth and panic classes; taint inside functions and interface-dispatched paths remain unanalysed
